test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 02 Aug, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, which has come into force on the 21st of April 2018, extends to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Whole of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018** was introduced as a means to deter **economic offenders** from evading the Indian legal system and fleeing the country.
 
• The Act allows for the **attachment and confiscation** of the properties of an individual who is declared a fugitive economic offender.
 
• The Act also establishes a** special court** to deal with such cases.
 
• The Act applies to any individual who has committed an offence involving an amount of **Rs 100 crore or more **and has fled the country to avoid prosecution.
 
• The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, which has come into force on the **21****st**** of April 2018**, extends to** whole of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018** is an important tool in combating economic offences and ensuring that offenders are held accountable for their actions.
 
• On **March 12, 2018**, the** Fugitive Economic Offenders Act's bill **was introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, and on **July 25, 2018,** it was passed.
 
• The Act also allows for the **provisional attachment of all of the offender's assets** and their ultimate confiscation upon the Special Court's designation of the offender as a fugitive economic offender.
